title: Teysuno and cisplatin for advanced gastric cancer
schedule_label: Teysuno twice daily on days 1–21, then seven days off. Cisplatin on day 1 every 28 days.
schedule_summary: Teysuno twice daily on days 1–21, then seven days off. Cisplatin on day 1 every 28 days. Cisplatin is planned for up to six cycles. If it stops early while the cancer is responding, the team may restart Teysuno alone once restart criteria are met.
purpose: Treatment aims to control advanced cancer and relieve symptoms. Your team will discuss benefit and side effects at review.
administration_text: IV fluids are given around cisplatin. Report reduced urine, tinnitus or hearing change. Take Teysuno with water at least one hour before or one hour after food. Keep a capsule diary and skip a vomited or missed dose.
monitoring_summary: Review blood counts, kidney function, electrolytes and liver tests before the next cycle. Check hearing, hydration and urine output.
review_status: Independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending.

agents.name: Teysuno (S-1)
agents.mechanism: Tegafur is converted to fluorouracil. Gimeracil slows its breakdown and oteracil modifies its activity in the gut.
agents.explanation: Tegafur is converted to fluorouracil. Gimeracil slows its breakdown and oteracil modifies its activity in the gut.
visual: Tegafur is converted to fluorouracil. Gimeracil slows its breakdown and oteracil modifies its activity in the gut.
agents.watch: Stop and contact the team for significant diarrhoea, fever, painful mouth ulcers or poor intake.
consent_risks: Report severe or early bowel or mouth symptoms urgently. DPD deficiency increases the risk of serious toxicity.
Seek emergency help for chest pain, severe breathlessness or collapse.
Use only the prescribed strengths. Leave a vomited or missed dose out and record it.

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.mechanism: Makes links in DNA that interfere with cell division.
agents.explanation: Makes links in DNA that interfere with cell division.
visual: Makes links in DNA that interfere with cell division.
agents.watch: Call the team for reduced urine, persistent vomiting or ringing in the ears.
consent_risks: IV fluids and blood tests protect the kidneys. Report reduced urine or dehydration.
Report ringing in the ears, hearing loss or numbness before the next treatment.
Take the prescribed anti-sickness cover. Call urgently if unable to drink or if you feel feverish.

common_effects.title: Mouth and bowel
common_effects.text: Ring for painful ulcers, persistent diarrhoea or inability to drink.

common_effects.title: Fatigue and appetite
common_effects.text: Tell the team about weight loss or difficulty swallowing so that nutrition support can be arranged.

common_effects.title: Fluid and hearing changes
common_effects.text: Report reduced urine or ringing in the ears.

serious_effects.title: Infection
serious_effects.text: Phone oncology immediately for fever, shivering or sudden illness. For severe chest pain, severe breathing difficulty or collapse call 112 or 999.

serious_effects.title: Chest pain
serious_effects.text: Fluoropyrimidines can affect blood flow to the heart. Seek emergency help for new severe chest pain.

serious_effects.title: Severe early toxicity
serious_effects.text: Contact oncology immediately for severe diarrhoea, mouth ulcers or fever early in a course.

evidence.title: FLAGS
evidence.interpretation: In previously untreated advanced gastric or junctional adenocarcinoma, median survival was 8.6 months with S-1/cisplatin and 7.9 months with infused fluorouracil/cisplatin. The trial did not demonstrate superiority (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.80–1.05).
evidence.limitations: These results describe selected trial populations. Your outlook depends on your disease, fitness and treatment setting.
